I don't pretend to understand the Great Game of geopolitics, but it's fun to think about it from a lot of different perspectives.

  • From the myopic US angle, I'm not sure how much the DNC leaks effected the election. They confirmed several existing Clinton scandals and cast a light on how Wassermann-Schultz fucked over Bernie Sanders. Without the DNC leaks, I'm fairly certain Trump would've still won. I'm not sure if Obama/DNC/intel community sees it that way, or if Russia is just a scapegoat for Clinton's historic loss. Ultimately, the leaks were a footnote in the election itself.

  • Russia is a big country. If it were a Russian group that hacked the DNC, that doesn't mean it was instigated by the Russian government. Someone inside the US may have hired them to do so, or a Russian group without ties to the government may have done so for some other reason.

  • If it was Putin's doing, and Trump's camp knew ahead of time or arranged it, then Trump would owe a favor to the Russian government. This would absolutely be interfering with US sovereignty, and Obama is right to take action. However, there's still the "pot calling the kettle cookware of color" here, since the US frequently intervenes in other elections (often cited: Obama campaigning against Netanyahu). Leaks are a more underhanded way of doing so, however...

  • These were leaks! No one's questioning the veracity of the info. No matter who is ultimately responsible for the information being available, these emails were actually sent by the Democratic party, and most of them (especially those that had to do with the way the DNC handled Sanders) were never addressed by the DNC. They are acting like just because the info was leaked by "Russians" they can pretend that it didn't reveal big problems with the Democratic party. Instead of addressing the source of the leaks, how about addressing the content?

  • Obama is casting doubt over Trump's legitimacy as president, and this is going to be an everpresent issue for the next 4-8 years that liberals keep bringing up. We're at a time when the country is more divided than ever, people are filled with hate and anger. Rather than try to heal the divide and set up for a stronger America, Obama is choosing a path right now that's petty and ultimately damaging to the US as a whole.

Note that I'm not saying that there shouldn't eventually be more of an investigation, and perhaps some sanctions if it does turn out that the Russian government was interfering in the US election, but now is not the time to do it. Right now, the job of the CIA and FBI is the strength of America as a whole, and this action does not strengthen America in the eyes of the rest of the world, and certainly does not strengthen America internally. I feel that no good can come of this action for America as a whole. But some good can come of it for the Democratic party, since it distracts from the content of the emails and casts doubt on Trump's legitimacy.

tl;dr: Obama is sacrificing the good of America for the good of the Democratic party.
